conditions.description: How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing. Learn more about program declaration Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

An Associate Certificate must contain a minimum of 30.0 credits and approved courses from the Associate Certificate can be incorporated into the requirements for a Certificate . conditions.description: How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Here is what I can verify from the current Asteris/BCIT program record for the **Civil Technology Associate Certificate**:

### Verified

- The program is an **active, part-time Associate Certificate** delivered in a blended format at Burnaby Campus/Online.
- The program is **under review and expected to undergo a curriculum change**.
- It is **not available to international students**.
- There is **no formal application process or requirement to register in the program to take individual courses**, provided you meet the applicable course prerequisites or have equivalent knowledge.
- To complete the certificate, you submit a **Program Declaration Request**. The declaration must be approved by the **Civil Engineering department**.
- The record states that, after approval, BCIT sends a **program plan letter** confirming the program of study. It also states that processing may take approximately **eight weeks**.
- The certificate requires **30.0 credits**, including:
  - A required-course component involving:
    - **CIVL 1120 — Statics**
    - **CIVL 1121 — Graphical Communication**
    - **CIVL 1160 — Applied Hydrology**
    - **COMM 1103 — Introduction to Business and Technical Communication**
    - **MATH 1013 — Advanced Technical Mathematics**
    - **MATH 1401 — Technical Mathematics for Architectural and Building Technology**
  - At least **9.5 credits from the approved elective pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses. The pool includes courses such as **AICO 1000 — AutoCAD 1**, **CIVL 2123 — Concrete Technology**, **SURV 1104 — Basic Surveying with Total Stations**, and others.
- The admission record lists:
  - English Studies 12 with 50% or equivalent.
  - Math 12 or **MATH 0001 — Technical Mathematics**, or equivalent, as the stated math requirement.
  - A note that Math 12 must have been completed with at least a C to receive credit for the relevant course, and that students whose Math 12 was completed more than five years ago are strongly recommended to begin with a required math course.

Because the program is under review, I recommend confirming:

1. Whether the certificate is currently accepting new international or domestic declarations.

Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Here is what I can verify from the current Asteris/BCIT program record for the **Civil Technology Associate Certificate**:

### Verified

- The program is an **active, part-time Associate Certificate** delivered in a blended format at Burnaby Campus/Online.
- The program is **under review and expected to undergo a curriculum change**.
- It is **not available to international students**.
- There is **no formal application process or requirement to register in the program to take individual courses**, provided you meet the applicable course prerequisites or have equivalent knowledge.
- To complete the certificate, you submit a **Program Declaration Request**. The declaration must be approved by the **Civil Engineering department**.
- The record states that, after approval, BCIT sends a **program plan letter** confirming the program of study. It also states that processing may take approximately **eight weeks**.
- The certificate requires **30.0 credits**, including:
  - A required-course component involving:
    - **CIVL 1120 — Statics**
    - **CIVL 1121 — Graphical Communication**
    - **CIVL 1160 — Applied Hydrology**
    - **COMM 1103 — Introduction to Business and Technical Communication**
    - **MATH 1013 — Advanced Technical Mathematics**
    - **MATH 1401 — Technical Mathematics for Architectural and Building Technology**
  - At least **9.5 credits from the approved elective pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses. The pool includes courses such as **AICO 1000 — AutoCAD 1**, **CIVL 2123 — Concrete Technology**, **SURV 1104 — Basic Surveying with Total Stations**, and others.
- The admission record lists:
  - English Studies 12 with 50% or equivalent.
  - Math 12 or **MATH 0001 — Technical Mathematics**, or equivalent, as the stated math requirement.
  - A note that Math 12 must have been completed with at least a C to receive credit for the relevant course, and that students whose Math 12 was completed more than five years ago are strongly recommended to begin with a required math course.

### Confirm directly with BCIT

Because the program is under review, I recommend confirming:

1. Whether the certificate is currently accepting new international or domestic declarations.
2. Whether the published curriculum and 30-credit structure will change, and which version would apply to you.
3. Exactly which courses in the required-course component must be completed and which are alternatives—the stored curriculum wording is not sufficiently clear to establish the precise combinations.
4. Whether any individual course you want requires departmental approval, additional acceptance, or a prerequisite assessment.
5. Whether your intended declaration has been approved and whether BCIT will issue your program plan letter.
6. Current declaration deadlines, fees, space availability, and processing timelines.
